messages:
alex: Heads up — prod cluster-prod-7 hit repeated TP scaling timeouts during the 2->4 node burst last night (around 21:08 UTC). Symptoms: per-rank allreduce waits, rendezvous partial failures, a bunch of requests timed out. This started after Tue's kernel-selector tweak (commit abc123). Anyone seen similar?

maya: Ugh. Do we have a small repro? Could be batching heuristic misaligning between nodes after the kernel change.

jun: I ran a quick profile on perf-run-2001. Flamegraphs show compute finishes earlier on some ranks while others spike on allreduce. Looks like comm/compute overlap got worse. Snippet from trace: 

```
[rank0] step 102: compute 12ms, allreduce 5ms
[rank1] step 102: compute 18ms, allreduce 120ms  <-- waiting
[rank2] step 102: compute 11ms, allreduce 6ms
[rank3] step 102: compute 10ms, allreduce 130ms  <-- stuck until rank1
```

jun: Full perf artifacts uploaded to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/2001/tp-scaling/ (see perf-run-2001/timeline.pb).

lina: Quick hypothesis: kernel-selector now prefers a FP16 kernel variant that has worse small-sequence throughput on older SMs. That makes some ranks slower on compute and causes the allreduce to wait. Also saw kv-cache warmup differences across hosts — some ranks have cold prefixes so they emit different micro-batch shapes.

alex: That matches logs — kv-cache misses on ranks 1 and 3 right before the stall in several traces. Could be two issues compounding: kernel latency skew + batch alignment mismatch due to KV cache warmup.

maya: Possible mitigations we can roll quickly: (A) pin model routing by user-id hash to keep prefixes on the same host (reduces KV-cache churn), (B) temporarily increase batching_max_delay to 8ms to allow batch alignment, (C) force previous kernel variant for the canary pool.

sre-bot: Incident INC-9872 created by alex: "tp scaling: allreduce timeouts after kernel-selector change" — assignees: eng-runtime oncall.

jun: I prepared a small revert PR that resets the kernel-selector threshold and keeps the fix gated behind an opt-in flag: https://git.internal/r/pr/4321 (shortlink). Also pushed a small allreduce guard: if per-rank batch_count variance > 1 then stagger collective start by up to 2ms to reduce head-of-line stalls.

lina: I'll run the staged repro on a 4-node staging cluster with KV-cache sync hook enabled and capture traces. Scheduling for 9:30 PT. I'll add the headroom metric to the dashboard (per-rank compute vs comm imbalance).

maya: +1 on the routing pinning mitigation as a quick rollback-in-place. Can we also add a short-lived telemetry counter for 'kvcache-miss-before-send' so we can correlate with timeouts?

alex: Action items: (1) jun -> open canary revert and deploy to canary pool, (2) lina -> run staged repro + gather perf, (3) maya -> implement routing pin for affected models and add telemetry counter. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:

lina: NOTE: repro shows slightly different behavior when seq_len > 512 vs <= 512 — the kernel choice changes at the sequence-length boundary. Might be a micro-kernel mismatch, not just FP type.

jun: If we can't revert quickly, quick opt-in on the runtime: KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDE=legacy for the canary hosts. I can push a hotfix image.

maya: Will also prepare a runbook snippet for oncall: how to detect batch-skew and apply the routing pin / kernel override.

alex: Thanks team. Keep short updates here; if we see a full cluster regression we escalate.
